name: Self-Directed Queries Complexity of Axis-Parallel Boxes
proof: Theorem 12 of \cite{devulapalli2024selfdirected} bounds the subset-maximized self-directed mistake complexity of real axis-aligned boxes by $2d$. Every nonempty grid box is the restriction of such a real box, so the same upper bound holds here. For $n\ge3$, take the $2d$ points $c\pm e_j$ around $c=(1,\ldots,1)$. For each labeling, the smallest box containing $c$ and the positively labeled points contains exactly those positives among the selected points; the negative-only labeling is realized by $\{c\}$. Thus these points are shattered and force $2d$ mistakes. For $n=2$, the $d$ unit vectors are shattered: the box spanned by zero and any selected unit vectors realizes precisely that selection. This gives the displayed lower bound; no exact value for this boundary is asserted here. The classical two-mistake result concerns prediction on the entire grid, not the maximum over its subsets.
references: \cite{devulapalli2024selfdirected}, Section 2.1 and Theorem 12; \cite{goldman1994power}, Theorem 4, concerns only the whole grid.
